title: Stateful canary orchestration for priv EKS control plane terraform module
creator: Aisha Martinez
description:
Goal: Introduce a stateful canary orchestration layer into the existing redwood_priv_eks control plane terraform module to support safe, reversible upgrades for Private (VPC) EKS control plane nodes. This ticket covers module design, preflight validations, canary rollout orchestration (Terraform-driven steps + operatorless hooks), automated health checks and rollback triggers, CI integration for terraform plans, and observability hooks for SLO/alerting.

Background: We've had several pain points during control plane upgrades: schema drift on CRDs, intermittent IAM token expiration after node replacements, and opaque failures during multi-AZ upgrades. Current provisioning modules are declarative but lack a recommended procedural canary for stateful pieces (etcd scale/restore patterns, k8s control-plane components).

Scope & deliverables:
- Design and implement a new submodule redwood_priv_eks::canary_orchestrator that emits an ordered set of upgrade steps (tf resources + null_resources with local-exec) while remaining compatible with our operatorless provisioning goals.
- Implement preflight_sentry validations: terraform plan validators and lightweight kubernetes probes that run after each step to assert health (API server L7 checks, etcd quorum verification, certificate validity check, node kubelet readiness).
- Add deterministic rollback markers and a checkpointing mechanism (S3-backed state markers encrypted with KMS) so partial upgrades can be resumed or rolled back by CI pipelines.
- Create automated chaos probes (non-destructive) that run in the canary path to ensure resilience: control-plane leader-election latency, small-scale etcd write/read verification.
- Integrate with release orchestration: a new pipeline job infra/priv-eks/canary-upgrade-run that sequences terraform apply for step N, triggers probes, evaluates pass/fail rules, and proceeds or runs rollback.
- Add telemetry: Grafana dashboard panels and alert rules for canary failures (link in comments).

Acceptance criteria:
- Module publishes a documented canary orchestration interface in the registry (inputs/outputs documented).
- Automated preflight validations are run by CI and gate terraform apply for at least two major upgrade scenarios.
- Canary pipeline can perform a staged upgrade across AZs and will automatically rollback on defined failure conditions within 10 minutes.
- Rollback marker + resume semantics verified in a simulated interrupted upgrade test.
- Observability: dashboard shows canary-run duration, step statuses, and aggregated health metrics; failure alerts wired to oncall channel.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Adding procedural steps reduces pure declarativity; mitigate by keeping default behavior as single-step apply and enabling canary_orchestrator via a boolean flag.
- S3/KMS markers increase infra surface area for state; document KMS key rotation policy and minimal IAM roles.

Implementation notes and design decisions:
- Use null_resource with triggers for running small, idempotent shell helpers (kubectl probes) where a full controller is not warranted. Helpers will be packaged as a small Docker image hosted in our ECR to ensure consistent tooling.
- Checkpoint markers are namespaced by cluster-id + upgrade-id; objects stored in s3://redwood-priv-eks-checkpoints/<cluster-id>/<upgrade-id>/state.json encrypted with a dedicated KMS key.
- Health checks use a mix of cluster-level (apiserver 200 on /healthz, kube-scheduler metrics) and data-integrity checks against a short-lived test namespace.
- Failure rules are pluggable: simple default (>=1 critical check fail OR API error rate spike > 50% over 3m) but teams can supply a custom evaluation lambda.

Compatibility matrix:
- Module must operate with terraform >= 1.4 and AWS provider >= 5.0.
- Backwards compatibility: when canary_orchestrator.enabled = false, behavior unchanged.

Open questions:
- Should the checkpoint KMS key be the customers' KMS or a Redwood-managed key for Hosted Private deployments? (Security asked for customer-managed by default.)
- What SLA do we want for the canary job runtime? Current design target is < 45m for typical control plane minor upgrades.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Canary+Orchestrator+for+priv+EKS
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4621
- E2E sim cluster job: infra/ci/jobs/priv-eks-canary-sim.yaml
